steps.action: Re-assessment of the Wwise code against the SDK headers. Found: (1) AK::SoundEngine::RenderAudio is never called; the header says it processes the command queue and 'has to be called periodically (usually once per game frame)'. (2) No listener is registered or set as default, so the debug emitter has no listener. (3) GetSourcePlayPosition needs AK_EnableGetSourcePlayPosition on PostEvent, which we never passed, so the 'ends at once' result in S-049 to S-060 was a test artefact. The device tests (S-051, S-057, S-059, S-060) looked in the wrong place. User approved fixing these (option A) and a clean sound backend interface (option B, new Phase 3; weapon fire becomes Phase 4)

steps.action: User asked whether channels relate to audio buses. Answer recorded: a channel is a per-emitter slot defined by the game (voice, body, weapon, item), used to stop or replace what one entity plays; it has no role in mixing. The bus-like concept is the shader's soundClass (FadeSoundClasses), which maps to Wwise buses in the project (§7, Phase 5). User approved the revised §8.4 ('let's go'). Starting P-04.2

decisions.decision: Wwise test content is built through the Wwise Authoring API (WAAPI, WwiseConsole waapi-server) by tools/wwise_test_project.js. Tab-delimited import cannot create events
decisions.reason: Tab-delimited import rejects events. WAAPI is the supported scripting route

decisions.decision: Phase 2 uses the SDK default I/O to load banks from base/wwise/Windows/ and a debug console command wwise_play for events. Banks are copied from the generated folder for the test; a build step for this is a later task
decisions.reason: Needed for the test. Keeps the game code path to one debug command
decisions.revisit: Phase 3 replaces the debug command with the game route

decisions.decision: Keep one build folder (build/, RelWithDebInfo). Other builds (Debug, OpenAL-only) are created on demand and deleted after use
decisions.reason: Disk space and clarity; the user asked for it
decisions.revisit: A debug investigation needs a second build

decisions.decision: Wwise gets the standard per-frame calls: RenderAudio once per sound tick, one listener game object set as the default listener, and the debug PostEvent asks for play-position tracking. For now this is called from idSoundSystemLocal::AsyncUpdate / AsyncUpdateWrite (dhewm3's existing sound tick)
decisions.reason: Required by the SDK (S-061). User approved option A
decisions.revisit: Phase 3 moves the call behind the backend interface

decisions.decision: OpenAL and Wwise go behind one sound backend interface (new Phase 3), even though OpenAL may be removed later. The interface design is written in these notes and approved by the user before any code. Weapon-fire routing moves to Phase 4
decisions.reason: User asked for a clean implementation (option B)

decisions.decision: Backend interface is sound.h (idSoundSystem, idSoundWorld, idSoundEmitter), one full provider per backend. A service locator (idSoundSystemLocator) picks the provider once at start-up and points the soundSystem pointer at it (option 1). The forwarding facade/proxy (option 2) was rejected. Features without a Wwise equivalent get neutral stubs and go to the triage list. Design in §8.3
decisions.reason: Textbook service-provider pattern; less code and no forwarding layer to maintain. Costs one changed line in framework/Common.cpp. Game DLL copies the pointer only after sound start-up
decisions.revisit: Backend must be switchable without a restart

decisions.decision: Positions are sent to Wwise in meters (DOOM_TO_METERS), axes converted to Wwise (X right, Y up, Z forward). Doom 3 sound shaders already give minDistance and maxDistance in meters, so Wwise attenuation curves use the same numbers
decisions.reason: Matches the shader data and the usual unit in Wwise projects; students author attenuation in meters

decisions.decision: Dashboard step log is sorted by step number and shows each step on two lines (date, phase and result; then the action). Phase 2 counts as done on the output capture; the user's listening check is part of P-04.4
decisions.reason: User feedback: the board still showed Phase 2 and was hard to read

decisions.decision: A sound shader plays the Wwise event named Play_<shader> (non-alphanumeric characters become _). Every StartSound posts its event; a missing event gives Wwise's console warning, and wwise_missing lists the shaders whose post failed. Code keeps only the sound.h channel contract (stop a channel, a new sound replaces the old one on its channel, CurrentlyPlaying); random choice, play-once, limits and looping are Wwise event setup. Phase 4 test content uses the original weapon-fire samples, extracted locally and never committed. Design in §8.4 (revision S-069)
decisions.reason: User answers to Q-07 and Q-08: missing-event warnings are normal game behaviour; sound behaviour belongs to the sound designer in Wwise. Students add events without code or data changes
decisions.status: Accepted (Q-07, Q-08; revision S-069 approved in S-070)

decisions.decision: StartSound returns the event's estimated duration (DurationMax) from the bank metadata (<bank>.json) that Wwise writes; 0 for looping, unknown or missing events. The metadata is only read for lengths, posting stays as D-052 (no existence check). Later step, not Phase 5: end-of-event callbacks (queued to the game thread) so the radio and PDA HUD icons follow the real end of the sound; markers for subtitles if needed
decisions.reason: Radio and PDA are important for gameplay; their voice lines are single samples, so the estimate is the real length (S-076, S-077). Keeps game code and Doom's scripts unchanged

decisions.decision: Run-time SSF_GLOBAL (speakers, game code) and the listener's own emitter: the sound is posted on a per-world game object kept at the listener, and stays tracked on the emitter's channel. Run-time SSF_OMNIDIRECTIONAL: RTPC_Spatialization on the playing ID (to be checked in P-05.3 that attenuation stays). One event per shader, no _global variants
decisions.reason: Wwise fixes 2D/3D per object at authoring; game code sets these flags at run time, so code is needed anyway (S-079)
decisions.revisit: P-05.3; attenuations get full spread at distance 0

decisions.decision: Wwise test project banks: one bank per Doom .sndshd file (107 for the base game, about 100 MB of source audio; Resurrection of Evil adds its own), all loaded at start. Students' projects may split banks differently; the provider loads the banks listed in a bank list
decisions.reason: Follows Id's own grouping; simple to find and replace a category (S-079)
